kind: analysis choices, cited thresholds and imaginary cases; nothing in this file is measured in the Demerzel repository
random_seed_note: The analysis draws no random numbers: every probability is an exact sum over a finite list of outcomes.

rounding.note: Probabilities, p-values, shares and interval bounds are rounded to 6 decimals; 'exact' is the unrounded fraction where it is short enough to print.

pinned_commit.note: Cited, not extracted: the committer date of the pinned commit, read once with `git show -s --format=%cI 4b03838800dcd4894f1e026461979bff1d985ca8` (2026-10-13T18:01:18-04:00). Used only to count the whole days since the last recorded cycle.

caught_statuses.note: An injection is counted as caught in a cycle when its status is one of these. The rule is read from the report of cycle chaos-003, whose 'Caught?' column says YES for exactly these two statuses (analyze.py checks that against the snapshot). Applying it to the other cycles is an analysis choice: the history itself does not state a rule.

level_keys.note: The history names levels 'L2' in the injection list and 'L2_binding' in level_scores. This maps one to the other.

test_family.note: The comparisons this module treats as one family for the multiple-comparison correction: the three consecutive steps and the first cycle against the last. The list is the one named in the coordinator's notes for this module; it was fixed before any p-value was computed, but after the four scores had been read. Indices are positions in the history (0 = first record).

smaller_family.note: The same family without the first-against-last comparison, to show what the size of the family does to the threshold.

fixed_rate_cases.note: Assumed detection rates for the questions 'how often do three independent cycles of the same size rise strictly under one fixed rate?' and 'how often does the policy's trend rule say improving?'. The pooled rate of the cycles being examined is added by analyze.py.

trend_rule.note: How this fixture reads the trend rule of policies/resilience-metric-policy.yaml ('Compare last 3 records'; improving when 'Latest R > average of previous 2', degrading when it is below, stable otherwise): with only one earlier record, the average is that record; with none, the label is 'stable'. The policy does not state these two cases.

regime_thresholds.source: PSY-002 (psy-002-governance-phase-transitions, pinned commit), section 'Signal 2: Health Score Velocity': regime thresholds on the resilience score R. Cited, not re-derived here; analyze.py checks that they are the cut points of the resilience metric policy.

imaginary_cases.note: Synthetic. None of these cycles or injection sets exists.

all_caught_on_the_reused_set.description: A fifth cycle that re-scores the same injections and records every one as caught.

held_out_sets.description: A fresh injection set written without knowledge of the fixes and scored once, compared with the last recorded cycle by a two-sided Fisher exact test. For each size, analyze.py finds the largest caught count that would still differ from the last cycle at the significance level.

one_regression.description: Negative control: a copy of the history in which one injection caught in the last cycle is marked missed again.

tea_tasting.source: Fisher, R. A. (1935), The Design of Experiments, chapter II: eight cups, four of each kind, 70 equally likely ways to choose four. One way gets all four right and 16 get three right, so 'three or more right' has probability 17/70. Doubling it for this symmetric table (34/70) is this fixture's arithmetic, not a figure from the book.

first_step.worked: 0 of 11 against 7 of 11: 7 caught among 22, so P(none of the 7 falls in the first cycle) = C(15,11) / C(22,11) = 1365 / 705432.

transfer_task.note: The learner task uses the second series of the same folder (the three red-team cycle files), read from observed-input.json. Only the analysis choices are set here.
transfer_task.expected_counts: the PASS counts recounted from each file's scenario list (the learner task prints that list); the counts of each file's own summary are computed as well, because two summaries disagree with their lists
